summary: Without a hard gate layer this pattern is simply merging unreviewed machine output, and the record, independence, status honesty and social functions of the pull request all have to be rebuilt somewhere else.

points.text: No gate infrastructure, no pattern. DORA's 2025 work reports that AI adoption raises throughput while stability degrades where validation systems lag behind the speed of the automation. Removing the human gate before the machine gates are trustworthy converts a review bottleneck into a change-failure problem.

Without a verifiable completion rule the board lies. The case-study system introduced its acceptance invariant only after cards had been stamped delivered from prose and a bulk acceptance of 35 cards reported no-branch on every sampled merge. If 'done' is not derived from git ancestry of attributed commits, skipping the diff read removes the last person who would have noticed.

Regulated environments may require a named human approver or documented four-eyes segregation of duties. Keep the pull request where an external rule demands it, and run the gates in front of it; a configured pull-request integration strategy that stays in human review until the merge is real is the compliant shape of this pattern.

Reviewer independence is not free. When the author agent, the review agent and any adversarial wave share a model family, prompt lineage, fixture or context bundle, their errors correlate and three green verdicts are close to one. Rotate models and prompts, keep deterministic checks that do not depend on a model at all, and keep a sampled human audit.

Code review at scale mostly transports knowledge, ownership and norms rather than defect finds. In an agent-first team those functions must be re-homed into specs, decision records and living documentation; if nothing takes them over, the codebase drifts architecturally and stylistically while every gate stays green.

Gates erode under delivery pressure. When a gate blocks, the cheapest local fix is to weaken the gate: lower the coverage floor, skip the flaky suite, downgrade a finding to advisory, set the override flag. Treat gate configuration, review standards and override rules as a protected, separately reviewed surface with their own change history.

Per-card gates buy attention with compute, and compute queues too. In the case-study system the full suite is the largest compute-bound stage per delivery, and the review lane's inflow is about twice its outflow when the coding fleet runs hot. A batch gate that runs one suite for a wave of deliveries is a documented proposal there, not a shipped feature; budget for this before removing the human queue.
Small teams with low change volume have no review bottleneck to solve. There, a fast human pull request is cheaper than building and maintaining gate, verdict and integration-record infrastructure.
